evals.prompt: Create a skill that summarizes my uncommitted git diff into 3-6 bullet points and flags risky changes (migrations, auth, deleted tests). It should fire when I ask for a summary of my changes. Put it in skills/.
evals.expected_output: Drafts right away (the brief is clear): SKILL.md with a third-person description and a concrete 'Use when', Scope with Does NOT, numbered steps, a fixed output format, red flags, done when; evals.json with 3-5 cases with evidence-only assertions (incl. a fixture diff); runs check_skill.py; replies with description, size, cases, assumptions, asks for approval and names skill-reviewer as next.
assertions: Drafts the SKILL.md in this reply instead of stopping to ask first
The description is third person with a concrete 'Use when' trigger about summarizing changes
Writes 3-5 eval cases, each with assertions, including at least one fixture or diff as input
Ends by asking for approval and naming skill-reviewer as the next step (does not grade its own skill)

evals.prompt: The description on my review skill never triggers. Tighten it so it fires when I finish a change or before merging.
evals.expected_output: Treats it as an edit: rewrites only the description into third-person 'what it does. Use when …' with the user's trigger words (finished a change, before merging, review my diff/PR); leaves the body and evals alone; shows the before/after.
assertions: Changes only the description, leaving the body untouched
The new description is third person, says what it does and has a concrete 'Use when' with trigger words such as finishing a change or before merging
Does not scaffold a new skill

evals.prompt: Make me a skill for productivity.
evals.expected_output: Does not draft. Asks ONE question offering 2-3 concrete skills it could be, each with its trigger.
assertions: Asks a single question rather than a list of questions
Offers 2-3 concrete candidate skills, each with when it would trigger

evals.prompt: Create a skill to format changelog entries in Keep a Changelog style, and skip the evals — it's obviously simple.
evals.expected_output: Drafts the skill and writes 3-5 eval cases anyway with a one-line reason (evals are required); SKILL.md stays short; scope + red flags present.
assertions: Writes 3-5 eval cases with assertions despite the request, with a short reason
Keeps the SKILL.md short (no background on what a changelog is) with Scope and Red flags sections
Does not lecture at length about why evals matter (one or two sentences at most)

evals.prompt: This commit-messages skill costs too many tokens. Slim it down without losing what it does.
evals.expected_output: Removes the background the model already knows (git history, why commits matter), inlines the two small references (or drops what the model knows of Conventional Commits) and removes the 'read X first' step; fixes the vague description with a Use when trigger; keeps the process lines (72-char imperative subject, why-body, ticket id from branch, show and ask before committing); states the size before/after.
assertions: Removes the background section the model already knows (git history, what a commit is)
Removes the 'read references first' step by inlining or dropping the two small reference files
Keeps the behaviour-changing rules: imperative subject <= 72 chars, ticket id from the branch name, show the message and ask before committing
Rewrites the description into third person with a concrete 'Use when' trigger
